title: Asset allocation and portfolio construction
body_md:
**Asset allocation** explains most of long-run portfolio variability, more than individual security picks.

## Approaches

| Approach | Idea |
|---|---|
| **Strategic** | Long-term target mix by risk and goal |
| **Tactical** | Short-term tilts around the strategic mix |
| **Goal-based** | A bucket per goal with its own mix |
| **Core and satellite** | Low-cost core plus selective satellites |

## Rules of thumb

- Equity share rises with horizon and risk capacity.
- Keep **emergency** and short-term money outside equity.
- Use **correlation**: combine assets that do not move together.

## Rebalancing

- **Calendar** (e.g. yearly) or **threshold** (e.g. drift of 5 percentage points).
- Consider tax and exit loads before selling; use new money to rebalance when possible.

## Risk and return

Diversification reduces unsystematic risk; **systematic (market) risk** remains.

> **Exam tip:** Strategic is the long-term plan; tactical is the short-term deviation.
example: A 60:40 portfolio drifts to 70:30 after an equity rally. The adviser sells 10 points of equity (or directs new money to debt) to return to the target.
say: We rebalance by rule, not by emotion.
Diversification lowers specific risk, not market risk.
never: Move everything to what did best this year.

check.why: Strategic allocation is the long-term policy mix.
Specific risk can be diversified away.

check.q: A threshold rebalancing rule triggers when:
check.why: Rebalance when the mix drifts beyond the band.
